veranderings.rede: 'Onkruid' is normally a collective noun, so 'n onkruid' reads oddly; 'n onkruidplant' names a single plant naturally.

veranderings.voor: suig ook water uit die grond op vir die plant
veranderings.na: suig ook water vir die plant uit die grond op
veranderings.rede: In Afrikaans the separable particle 'op' closes the clause; 'vir die plant' after it reads as a tacked-on afterthought.
'Sade begin' used intransitively like this reads as a calque of English 'seeds begin'; 'ontstaan' says the same thing idiomatically.
'daar binne-in' is clumsy; the adverb 'daarbinne' (one word) is the natural form here.

veranderings.blok: Wat die vrug en die saad doen
veranderings.voor: en los die sade ver weg
veranderings.na: en laat die sade ver weg agter
veranderings.rede: 'los die sade ver weg' is colloquial and unclear; 'laat ... agter' is the standard idiom for leaving something behind somewhere.

veranderings.voor: Die deel wat water na die blare dra
veranderings.na: Die deel van 'n plant wat water na die blare dra
veranderings.rede: A glossary entry is read on its own, so 'Die deel' needs to say what it is a part of; this may touch a shared definition, so the reviewer may prefer to route it.
